comparison: Perfect agreement on acentrosomal cell generation methods (C24-C27, C29-C30). Both evaluations find the methodology sound and well-validated. Peer reviewer explicitly notes this as a strength, and OpenEval confirms appropriate controls and quantification.

Strong agreement on the basic observation of elongated mitosis in acentrosomal cells (C3, C32-C34). Both evaluations accept the finding that NEBD-to-anaphase period is elongated. Editor and reviewers acknowledge this as a convincing observation without dispute.

Significant disagreement on interpretation of MPS1 inhibition experiments (C4, C38-C42). OpenEval finds strong evidence that MPS1 activity enforces SAC-mediated delay. Peer Reviewer 2 raises substantial concerns that 'results are not conclusive' and notes other MPS1 functions haven't been ruled out, requesting additional mechanistic data.

Agreement on the basic observations of monopolar spindles and division failure (C43-C44, C46-C47). Peer reviewer acknowledges MTOC formation characterization as interesting and notes monopolar spindles are not disputed, though requests more mechanistic detail about what happens during MPS1 inhibition.

Complete agreement on the reversibility control (C48). Both evaluations accept this demonstrates phenotypes are specifically due to centrosome loss rather than off-target effects. No reviewer challenges this important control experiment.

Disagreement on interpretation of proTAME rescue experiments (C49-C51, C59-C62). OpenEval finds strong mechanistic evidence that timing is critical. Peer Reviewer 2 finds results 'intriguing, but hard to interpret' and questions the mechanism, noting lack of clarity on why APC inhibition rescues MPS1 inhibition.

Disagreement on Aurora B inhibition experiments (C54-C58). OpenEval interprets these as supporting temporal interpretation. Peer Reviewer 2 raises critical concern that Aurora B requirement for SAC suggests MPS1 effect may be a non-SAC function, undermining the SAC-specific interpretation.

Strong agreement on polyploidy control experiments (C6-C7, C65, C68, C70-C72). Both evaluations accept that polyploidy has been ruled out as the causative factor. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges this as part of the experimental logic without challenge.

Partial overlap on temporal MTOC establishment (C73-C74 shared). OpenEval finds this directly supports mechanistic interpretation. Peer results focus more on STLC experiments (C9, C75-C77, C80, C89, C91) where Reviewer 2 notes multiple interpretations are possible and doesn't definitively accept the SAC-specific conclusion.

Disagreement on STLC experiments (C9, C75-C80). OpenEval finds strong evidence that monopolar spindle configuration drives SAC requirement. Peer Reviewer 1 finds this supports the model, but Reviewer 2 emphasizes 'multiple interpretations' exist and this doesn't definitively show MPS1 effect is SAC-related.

Qualified agreement on main conclusions (C10, C81-C83). OpenEval finds the 'timely two-ness' model well-supported by all experiments. Peer Reviewer 1 finds the model 'compelling' but requests additional experiments to strengthen the 'two-ness' conclusion, suggesting testing cells with only one centrosome. Reviewer 2 expresses substantial doubt about the SAC-specific interpretation.

Overlap on C81 regarding SAC-mediated delay requirement (C5, C8, C58, C81). OpenEval supports the conclusion strongly. Peer Reviewer 1 finds data consistent with the model, but Reviewer 2 states results are 'not conclusive' and emphasizes multiple interpretations exist.
OpenEval evaluates cell line characterization (C45) as appropriately documented with comprehensive validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological claim.
OpenEval finds the acknowledgment of unresolved questions (C84) appropriate and reasonable. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this limitation statement.
OpenEval rates translational speculation (C88) as UNCERTAIN, noting it extends beyond experimental data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific clinical speculation.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background literature claims (C1-C2, C11-C23, C28, C31, C35-C37, C50, C52-C53, C63-C64, C66-C67, C69, C85-C87, C89) as accurately represented. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual citations.
OpenEval evaluates hypothesis formulation and testing (C90-C91) as well-designed. Peer reviews discuss the STLC experiments but don't separately evaluate the hypothesis generation process.
